trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Going down would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
Going left would strand number 2: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,2). So the line goes left.
Going up would wall in number 11, the last number; going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going up would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (1,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left would cut off the top-left corner (4 cells). So the line goes down.
Going left would cut off the top-left corner (5 cells); going down would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
The line must go right: down is number 8, which comes later.
Cell (4,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.

Number 8 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going left would cut off the bottom-left corner (4 cells). So the line goes down.
Cell (6,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
